decisions.rationale: Von Hippel-Lindau disease is a single defined disease entity with no further categorization, annotated as the full string in the title.
Renal cell carcinoma is a single defined tumour type with no further subdivision in the title.
Repeated full name of Von Hippel-Lindau disease in the abstract; duplicate mentions are each annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 4 - Duplicate mentions; What to Annotate 1 - Specific Disease

decisions.rationale: VHL is the abbreviation of Von Hippel-Lindau disease and is annotated as a separate synonymous mention.
Autosomal dominant disorder refers to a family of multiple diseases defined by inheritance pattern, analogous to the autosomal recessive disease example.
Cancer is a retained general term that refers to a family of multiple specific cancers in 'various forms of cancer'.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 - General terms (cancer retained); What to Annotate 1 - Disease Class

decisions.rationale: Hemangioblastoma is a single specific tumour entity with no further categorization.
Phaeochromocytoma is a single specific tumour entity with no further categorization.
Pancreatic malignancies refers to a family of multiple pancreatic cancers rather than one specific disease.
Renal cell carcinomas (plural) refers to the single specific renal carcinoma entity.
Renal cell carcinomas at the start of a sentence refers to the same single specific disease as the previous mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 - Specific Disease; What to Annotate 4 - Duplicate mentions

decisions.rationale: Standalone disorder is a very general term comparable to disease or syndrome and is excluded.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 - General terms

decisions.rationale: Tumours here refers to a family of renal tumours in bilateral and multifocal presentation; tumour is a retained term and this is a head noun, not a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (tumour retained); What to Annotate 1 - Disease Class

decisions.rationale: In 'this tumour type', tumour is a disease term modifying the noun type, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
VHL is a disease abbreviation used as a modifier of the noun gene in 'the VHL gene'.
VHL modifies the noun locus in 'the VHL locus', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
VHL modifies the noun phenotype in 'the VHL phenotype', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
Tumour formation refers to a biological process (equivalent to tumorigenesis), not to a disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 5 - Biological processes

decisions.rationale: Tumour suppressor names a class of genes with a protective function, not a disease, so the tumour term is not a disease mention used as a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 5 - Biological processes; What to Annotate 3 applies only to disease mentions

decisions.rationale: The cancer refers generically to the family of renal cancers; cancer is a retained general term.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (cancer retained); What to Annotate 1 - Disease Class

decisions.rationale: Renal cell carcinomas refers to the single specific renal carcinoma entity in this sentence.
VHL-associated is a disease mention used as a modifier of the noun forms in 'VHL-associated forms of renal cell carcinoma'.
Renal cell carcinoma is a single specific disease in 'forms of renal cell carcinoma'.
Tumour in tumour suppressor gene names a gene class rather than a disease, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 5 - Biological processes; What to Annotate 3 applies only to disease mentions
